---
title: Round 8 referee calculations
---

At fixed liquid inventory, $G^*=G_{\rm EOS}+RT\sum_i n_i b_i(T,P_s)$ and
$G^*_P=V_{\rm EOS}+RT\sum_i n_i b_{i,P_s}\,dP_s/dP$.
R1–R3 track pressure. R4–R5 use 0.1 MPa where present.
Stationarity gives the same envelope derivative on each differentiable reaction branch at fixed conserved feed.
Sum phase contributions for a pair and use one-sided derivatives at a branch switch.
At fixed volume the separate pressure-reference chain term is
$-RT^2\sum_i n_i b_{i,P_s}(\partial P/\partial T)_{V,n}$.
The Gibbs–Helmholtz readback holds system and reference pressure fixed and uses the Engine caloric gauge through $G=H-TS$.
The phase volumes and energies are per mole of apparent amine fed.

Peiper and Pitzer Table 6 and Eq. 25 give $-\ln a_w/M_w=\phi_{\rm eq}\sum_i m_i=\phi_{\rm st}\sum_s\nu_s m_s$
within printed precision. The fitted ionic target subtracts the ideal dissolved CO₂ molality from the equilibrium numerator
and divides by the charge-closed ionic molality sum. The retained mixed denominator is 39 of 45.

These results await delivered evidence review and investigator promotion. The finite searches concern declared states and trial banks.
Measured property errors and predicted phase splits have separate evidentiary roles.

## Scope and provenance

The reference derivatives cover one fitted loading per amine and the parent and
two daughters at the extrapolated MDEA split. No comparison-pressure state
enters the derivative summary. The MEA and AMP caloric diagnostics remain
unresolved. The 100 kPa reference control at 204.054 MPa retains a resolved
descent. Its seeded two-liquid solve reports an indeterminate reduced Hessian
and returns no phase amounts for a bulk Gibbs comparison.

The AMP measured-pressure comparison retains the six exact historical controls
and their replay outcomes. The adopted refit includes 18 supplemental Hartono
and 40 loaded Tong pressures. The earlier hot-pressure biases were −28.1% for
18 Hartono and −25.3% for 25 Tong observations. The original model was also
sensitive to freezing or continuing R5 at constant enthalpy above 353.22 K.
These changes support a comparison of the complete refit and a separate
sensitivity of the original model.

The Weiland et al. (1998) Table 2 observations come from prepared solutions
measured with calibrated hydrometers. The phase splits are model predictions
at four of those feeds. The first split record gives both daughter amount
fractions, compositions, molar and mass densities, and the closure residuals.

The 82 current-model Kuranov predictions are row matched. Author aggregates
remain count-matched unless their row identities are established. The corrected
Kamps published values retain their 28-observation denominator. The comparable
local subset excludes Ermatchkov Table 6 row 13, where both pressure-weighted
solves exhausted their iterations. Hong equal-fugacity calculations fix the
vapor amount at $10^{-9}$ of the feed.

Core contributors are read from `be37c32a3`. The named display replays are
read from `be3e316c5`. The display contributor digests use decompressed JSON for gzip records.
The pinned-wheel readback independently reproduces the archived Kuranov
row 72 prediction of 1,165,619.52995 Pa at the same feed and temperature.

The branch adds 650 executable lines against `be37c32a3`, with six removed.
The initial 450-line estimate did not cover the same-gauge branch calculations,
matched witness and missing bubble-pressure readbacks, and reconstruction
checks for seven items. The owner authorized the expanded estimate. The
calculation reuses the round-7 reference, equilibrium, root, and coexistence
routines.
